summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit Intransitive (PrS 33/55)

data.turoyo: Ḥzele a tre tartemeniye klen miṯe, koṯe reḥo pis menayye, natini.
data.translation: Dort sah er die beiden Unholde todt liegen; ein hässlicher Geruch ging von ihnen aus, sie waren in Verwesung.

rationale: Thin Preterit Intransitive cell; plural state bearers and an overt bad-smell clause support stinking, without inventing a decay sense from German.

summary: All three occurrences retain the established stinken sense. Preterit Intransitive natən/natini describes an ambient or bodily state, while natino is an adjective-like Part act. predicate in a relative clause.
The market is a non-agentive state bearer, with mu reḥo da qṭile as cause/source. The two dead giants are plural state bearers; koṯe reḥo pis menayye explicitly supports the smell reading.
German waren in Verwesung names the condition associated with the smell at PrS 33/55; it does not establish a separate lexical rot/decompose sense.
The inherited market quotation and the straw quotation are not repeated. PrS 19/29 versus prs 47/10 remains a numbering-concordance question.
Verify whether inherited prs 47/10 and supplied PrS 19/29 are alternative edition references for the same market quotation before changing the citation.
Restore the adjective ending: hässlich → hässliche
rationale: The adjective modifying feminine nominative Stute after eine requires -e. The supplied edition translation repeats the missing ending, but it is an evident German typo.
